top_choice_rationale: Biomolecular condensates as liquid-liquid phase separation are a general physical-chemical principle of intracellular organisation, anchored in the 2009 P-granule work and the 2012 multivalent in vitro reconstitution, and replicated for fifteen years. Credit to Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen is imperfect (Pappu and Mittag are left out, and in vivo relevance of some condensates is debated), so P001 is a close and more attribution-clean second; P002 ranks third because its base-editing part has unresolved credit (Liu vs Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida), and no award is last.
recusal_note: Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Peter Somfai, and my lipid self-assembly and amyloid research is close to condensate biophysics, but no collaboration with the proposed laureates; no recusal required.
